author: independent SQL/PostgreSQL/JDBC SME critic subagent; did not author the reviewed artifacts

findings.claim: The validation summary is honest about its method but not adequate for a graded final. It does not say which 15 items ran on SQLite and which 13 are docs-only, or which PostgreSQL-vs-SQLite differences were neutralised beyond default NULL ordering. SQLite and PostgreSQL differ in general ways that bear on several of the planned SQL and transaction item types: error behaviour, foreign-key enforcement defaults, how script runners treat a failed statement, type affinity, numeric result types, casts, rounding and display, NULL ordering inside window definitions, visibility between sessions, and transaction-abort behaviour. No PostgreSQL error text can be reproduced on SQLite. The record also says no PostgreSQL server was available, yet the taught pages state their results were confirmed on PostgreSQL 17.5/18 servers.
findings.recommendation: Add a value-free validation method per planned id to the coverage map or this record, and list the engine settings and emulations used. The item must not key on behaviour that differs between engines unless it is checked against PostgreSQL documentation or a PostgreSQL run. Treat every PostgreSQL error branch and every quoted psql output as docs-checked, not executed. Before release, run the SQL items once on a real PostgreSQL 18 server (and the JDBC items against pgJDBC 42.7), or record them as unverified.

findings.claim: mcq-09's plan (a NULL-sensitive count with several near-miss options, also eliciting handling-nulls#o2) can easily end up with two correct keys. More than one formulation is semantically equivalent across every NULL case, and at least one such formulation is not taught on any course page.
findings.recommendation: Confirm privately that exactly one option is correct under the taught rules for every NULL case. Each distractor should be plausible under the taught rule but really wrong, and no untaught operator should appear.

findings.claim: mcq-18 (a top-per-group report that drops ties; choose the repair) risks two keys. The tie-handling functions taught on the window page can return identical rows at some cutoffs and differ only at others. A NULL in the ranked column also changes the result under PostgreSQL's NULL ordering.
findings.recommendation: Confirm privately that, for the item's data and cutoff, exactly one option meets the stated requirement. State or guarantee the NULL behaviour of the ranked column.

findings.claim: No course page teaches AND/OR operator precedence: a grep of every artifact.md for precedence, 'binds tighter' or parentheses rules finds nothing, and filtering-and-sorting only shows simple AND or OR. Several planned items combine OR with other conditions: mcq-08 (a filter that keeps a NULL group), mcq-09 (its count condition), mcq-06 (a preview SELECT that does not match its UPDATE) and mcq-25 (an input injected into a WHERE). If a keyed outcome depends on 'a AND b OR c' grouping as '(a AND b) OR c' without parentheses, it needs untaught material.
findings.recommendation: In mcq-06, -08, -09 and -25, put explicit parentheses around every mixed AND/OR, or keep each WHERE to a single operator, so the outcome follows from taught rules. If precedence is the intended pivot, teach it on filtering-and-sorting first.

findings.claim: Some contexts may imply surface text the pages do not show, which itemConstraints[0] forbids ('every API, error text and psql command in an item appears on a course page'). mcq-01: some psql output text, prompt forms and meta-commands appear on no page; installing-postgres teaches a limited set. mcq-29: the page describes the relevant symptom only in its own words, with no server error message. mcq-25: some SQL syntax for crafted inputs is untaught, and how the driver reports counts for some inputs depends on the driver.
findings.recommendation: Check the private items for mcq-01, -25 and -29 against the page wording. Describe symptoms the way the pages do, and show only messages, syntax and commands that a page shows.

findings.claim: An earlier plan line for mcq-11 disclosed the deciding fact; that line has since been removed.
findings.recommendation: Word displayed numeric values so they are valid for PostgreSQL's output and the taught rules. Never copy SQLite-rendered digits.

findings.claim: Some plannedContext and stepUp lines (in the plan version reviewed, among them mcq-14, mcq-21, mcq-22 and mcq-26) name the deciding fact of their item, close to stating the keyed reasoning. For mcq-21, the planned key also repeated a pattern a course page already shows in its own cheat sheet, so its step-up added little. This file is authoring evidence and not exported to learners, so the risk is small.
findings.recommendation: Reword those plannedContext and stepUp lines abstractly so that none names the fact that decides its item. Give mcq-21 a real step-up beyond any pattern a course page already shows.

findings.claim: In the plan version reviewed, the mcq-12 plannedContext described its second filtering stage ambiguously, so it did not clearly describe the three-stage grouped trace that its stepUp names.
findings.recommendation: Reword the mcq-12 plannedContext so that it names each stage's clause explicitly.
